ai.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines are a type of artificial intelligence technology that combines the strengths of retrieval-based and generative models to extract, summarize, and generate information from large datasets.
ai.howItWorks: RAG pipelines work by first retrieving relevant documents or passages from a knowledge base using a retrieval model. Then, a generative model is used to process these retrieved documents and produce context-aware responses or summaries.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the limitations of pure generative models in terms of accuracy and relevance by integrating them with retrieval models to ensure that generated content is grounded in factual information from reliable sources.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training both retrieval and generation models, integrating them into a pipeline architecture, and continuously fine-tuning these models based on feedback and new data.
ai.buildProcess: Models are built using large-scale datasets and advanced machine learning techniques. The process includes data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and deployment.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the acquisition and maintenance of large datasets, computational resources for training models, and continuous fine-tuning efforts to improve performance.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as RAG pipelines are increasingly being adopted in conversational AI systems, but there is still room for improvement in terms of efficiency and scalability.
ai.regulation: Regulations around data privacy, content accuracy, and ethical use of AI models need to be considered. Current frameworks vary by region, with some focusing more on transparency and accountability than others.
ai.risks: Risks include potential biases in the training data leading to biased outputs, challenges in maintaining model performance over time due to shifting language patterns, and concerns about data privacy and security.
ai.profitability: Profitability is contingent upon successful integration into commercial applications such as customer service chatbots, virtual assistants, and knowledge management systems. The market potential is significant but requires careful cost management.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving model efficiency, reducing latency in response times, enhancing cross-lingual capabilities, and addressing ethical concerns related to AI use.

glossary.def: A method in artificial intelligence that combines retrieval-based and generative models for information extraction, summarization, and response generation.
A structured collection of data used to provide context and factual support for AI-generated content.

subsystems.name: Ingestion and chunking
subsystems.role: turns raw documents into clean, searchable passages.
parts: document loaders for PDFs, HTML, databases
chunkers that split by length or structure

subsystems.name: Embedding model
subsystems.role: converts each passage into a vector that captures its meaning.

subsystems.name: Vector index
subsystems.role: stores vectors and finds the closest matches to a query quickly.

subsystems.name: Retriever and reranker
subsystems.role: selects the most relevant passages for a given question.

subsystems.name: Generator
subsystems.role: writes an answer using the retrieved passages as context.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and evaluation
subsystems.role: runs the pipeline and measures whether answers are correct and grounded.

buildSteps.title: Collect source documents
buildSteps.detail: Gather the knowledge base: PDFs, web pages, databases, tickets. Clean formatting and remove boilerplate.

buildSteps.title: Split into chunks
buildSteps.detail: Break documents into passages of a few hundred tokens, with overlap so meaning is not cut off at the edges.

buildSteps.title: Generate embeddings
buildSteps.detail: Run every chunk through an embedding model to produce a vector, typically hundreds of dimensions.

buildSteps.title: Build the vector index
buildSteps.detail: Load vectors into a vector database and build an approximate nearest-neighbour index for fast search.

buildSteps.title: Implement retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Encode the user query with the same embedding model, search the index, and return the top passages. Add metadata filters or a reranker to improve precision.

buildSteps.title: Connect the generator
buildSteps.detail: Design a prompt that inserts the retrieved passages and the question into a large language model, and instruct it to answer only from that context.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and tune
buildSteps.detail: Measure retrieval hit rate and answer faithfulness on a test set. Adjust chunk size, embedding model, number of passages retrieved, and prompt wording.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Serve the pipeline as an API or application. Monitor latency, cost and answer quality; re-index when source documents change.

pathway.milestone: basic RAG with a single vector store and simple top-k retrieval
pathway.unlocks: chat assistants that can answer questions over a company's private documents.

pathway.milestone: hybrid retrieval combining keyword and vector search, plus reranking and query expansion
pathway.unlocks: higher accuracy and fewer missed passages in technical or legal domains.

pathway.milestone: multi-step or agentic retrieval that breaks a question into sub-queries and iterates
pathway.unlocks: answering complex questions that need facts from several documents.

pathway.milestone: self-improving pipelines that learn from user feedback and combine vector stores with knowledge graphs
pathway.unlocks: knowledge systems that stay current and explain their reasoning.
